stem: A nurse is reviewing fasting instructions with a client before an elective procedure requiring anesthesia. Which client statement indicates correct understanding?

options.A: I will follow the specific eating and drinking instructions from my surgical and anesthesia team and will tell them if I do not follow those instructions exactly
options.B: Everyone having anesthesia follows one identical fasting schedule, so my medications and medical conditions do not affect the plan
options.C: If I accidentally eat or drink outside the instructions, I should not mention it unless I develop nausea
options.D: Fasting instructions are mainly for convenience and do not affect aspiration risk during anesthesia or deep sedation

rationale: Preprocedure fasting reduces aspiration risk during anesthesia or deep sedation. Instructions can vary with intake, procedure, anesthesia plan, medications and conditions affecting gastric emptying. Clients should follow individualized instructions and disclose deviations so the anesthesia team can reassess safety.
educational_objective: Teach clients to follow individualized preanesthesia fasting instructions and report deviations because fasting requirements are not identical for every client.
source_document_title: Preparing for Surgery — Adult Checklist / ASA patient guidance
source_locator: Pre-surgery directions and diet: follow surgical-team instructions; fasting addresses aspiration risk; clear-liquid allowances and special-risk plans may differ.
source_claim_supported: Clients should follow their specific fasting instructions and disclose deviations because aspiration risk and the appropriate plan vary with clinical circumstances.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing
blueprint_locator: Health Promotion and Maintenance — client education and risk reduction before procedures
blueprint_topic: Health Promotion and Maintenance — preoperative fasting education
correction_summary: Removed the quasi-universal two-hour clear-liquid rule and rebuilt the item around individualized instructions and disclosure of deviations, preserving accuracy for medications or conditions that alter gastric emptying.
audit_reviewer: OpenAI GPT-5.6 Sol — Rule 1 clinical audit + adversarial second pass

audit_findings.source_audit: Current ASA patient guidance and 2026-relevant delayed-gastric-emptying considerations checked.
audit_findings.claim_by_claim: Aspiration rationale, individualized instructions and disclosure of deviation are supported without universal interval.
audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only A is safe and universally applicable.
audit_findings.independent_adversarial_second_pass: Checked liquids, solids, GLP-1 therapy, diabetes, delayed gastric emptying and local policy; no unresolved conflict.
